findings.title: Which publisher is serving the live site
findings.detail: Served by the committed root fallback (legacy `main:/` Pages build), revision `88b1b2c3b96954e64f614ad08342cc74aeb289fe`. Snapshot age at read time 91.99 h; age when built -0.00 h. HEAD `6bfc034d33f7`, committed root receipt `88b1b2c3b969`. The legacy publisher is serving the committed fallback instead of the fresh artifact: this is the documented dual-publisher race, and the board a visitor reads is not the board the last verified run produced.

findings.title: The live board is outside its 8-hour evidence window
findings.detail: The served snapshot is 91.99 h old (generated `2026-10-18T00:52:19.597023Z`, read `2026-10-21T20:51:44.660459Z`). Every percentage on the live site is expired evidence and must not be used as a current pick. This is a publication-state finding, not a data finding: the next verified `pages.yml` run restores the fresh artifact.

findings.title: How the live open rows are priced
The deployed freshness copy matches the served snapshot
findings.detail: Snapshot `2026-10-18T00:52:19.597023Z` is 91.99 h old at read time and the strip says stale=True, so the copy and the data agree. Client-side expiry hook (assets/app.js `live-expired` + #runtime-stale) ships, so a row whose deadline passes while the page is open is re-expired in the browser.

findings.title: Render-time fingerprint of the served HTML
findings.detail: Strip says stale=True; receipt age at read time 91.99 h; receipt age at its own `built_at` -0.00 h. A strip that is stale while the receipt is not proves the HTML was rendered after the snapshot it carries.
